title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
titleEn: The Merchant and His Sons ends / King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān begins
part: Night 45 · The Merchant and His Sons ends / King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān begins
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 350–355 (Night 45, continuing directly from nights-44), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 45 closes the tale of Ghānim: the Caliph marries Fitna, Ghānim marries Qūt al-Qulūb, and the story is ordered written down for posterity. Shahrazād then begins the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān of Baghdad, his son Sharkān, and the twins Ḍawʾ al-Makān and Nuzhat al-Zamān born to the Byzantine slave-girl Ṣafiyya; the night ends as envoys of the king of Constantinople ask for ʿUmar’s help in a war, and morning overtakes Shahrazād. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْخَامِسَةُ وَالْأَرْبَعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-khāmisatu wa-al-arbaʿūna
sentences.l: And-when was the-night the-fifth and-the-forty.
sentences.i: And when it was the forty-fifth night,
sentences.n: The night formula. The ordinal is built “the fifth and the forty”, unit first, as in Night 44; the tens word الأربعون is in the nominative, agreeing with الليلة. We vocalise what is printed. The sentence is left open: its main clause is the next unit, قالت.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ غَانِمَ بْنَ أَيُّوبَ لَمَّا أَعْجَبَ الْخَلِيفَةَ فَصَاحَتُهُ وَنَظْمُهُ وَعُذُوبَةُ مَنْطِقِهِ قَالَ لَهُ اُدْنُ مِنِّي فَدَنَا مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna Ghānima ibna Ayyūba lammā aʿjaba al-khalīfata faṣāḥatuhu wa-naẓmuhu wa-ʿudhūbatu manṭiqihi qāla lahu udnu minnī fa-danā minhu
sentences.l: She-said: It-reached-me, O-you the-king the-felicitous, that Ghānim son-of Ayyūb, when pleased the-caliph his-eloquence and-his-ordering-of-words and-the-sweetness-of his-speech, said to-him: Draw-near from-me! So-he-drew-near from-him.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the caliph, delighted by Ghānim son of Ayyūb's eloquence, his fine phrasing and the sweetness of his speech, said to him: Come close to me. And Ghānim drew near.
sentences.n: The printed السعيدان is one word: the vocative's السعيد run together with أنّ (“that”), a print slip, as in Night 44. We keep the letters as printed and vocalise السعيد + أنّ. In لما أعجب الخليفة فصاحته the verb takes the caliph as its object and the eloquence as its subject (“his eloquence pleased the caliph”), which is why الخليفة is accusative and فصاحته nominative. The caliph is the unnamed subject of قال له, and Ghānim of فدنا.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ اِشْرَحْ لِي قِصَّتَكَ وَأَطْلِعْنِي عَلَى حِكَايَتِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla lahu ishraḥ lī qiṣṣataka wa-aṭliʿnī ʿalā ḥikāyatika
sentences.l: Then he-said to-him: Open-out to-me your-story and-make-me-informed upon your-tale.
sentences.i: Then he said to him: Lay out your story for me, and acquaint me with your tale.

sentences.t: فَقَعَدَ وَحَدَّثَ الْخَلِيفَةَ بِمَاجَرَى لَهُ فِي بَغْدَادَ وَبِنِيَامِهِ فِى التُّرْبَةِ وَأَخْذِ الصُّنْدُوقِ مِنَ الْعَبِيدِ بَعْدَ مَا ذَهَبُوا وَأَخْبَرَهُ بِمَاجَرَى لَهُ مِنَ الْمُبْتَدَأِ إِلَى الْمُنْتَهَى وَلَيْسَ فِى الْإِعَادَةِ إِفَادَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qaʿada wa-ḥaddatha al-khalīfata bi-mājarā lahu fī Baghdāda wa-bi-niyāmihi fī al-turbati wa-akhdhi al-ṣundūqi mina al-ʿabīdi baʿda mā dhahabū wa-akhbarahu bi-mājarā lahu mina al-mubtadaʾi ilā al-muntahā wa-laysa fī al-iʿādati ifādatun
sentences.l: So-he-sat and-recounted-to the-caliph of-whatever-befell to-him in Baghdad, and-of-his-sleeping in the-tomb, and-of-the-taking-of the-chest from the-slaves after what they-went, and-informed-him of-whatever-befell to-him from the-beginning to the-end; and-not-is in the-repeating any-benefit.
sentences.i: So he sat down and told the caliph all that had befallen him in Baghdad, how he had slept in the tomb, and how he had taken the chest from the slaves after they had gone; and he related to him everything that had happened to him from beginning to end. There is no profit in repeating it.
sentences.n: بماجرى is printed as one word: بما جرى, “of what befell”, with بـ because حدّث and أخبر take their subject-matter with بِـ (“tell of”). وبنيامه (“and of his sleeping”) is also governed by that بـ; نِيَام is read here as a verbal noun, “sleep”, where Classical has نَوْم (the form is not common in this use, so the reading is ours). وأخذ الصندوق is likewise a genitive verbal noun: “and of the taking of the chest”. The last clause is the narrator’s aside, declining to repeat what the listener has already heard. المبتدأ keeps the hamza the edition itself prints.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَلِمَ الْخَلِيفَةُ أَنَّهُ صَادِقٌ خَلَعَ عَلَيْهِ وَقَرَّبَهُ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿalima al-khalīfatu annahu ṣādiqun khalaʿa ʿalayhi wa-qarrabahu ilayhi
sentences.l: And-when knew the-caliph that-he truthful, he-removed upon-him and-brought-him-near to-him.
sentences.i: When the caliph knew that he spoke the truth, he bestowed a robe of honour upon him and drew him close.
sentences.n: خلع عليه, literally “he took off upon him”, is the set phrase for bestowing a robe of honour (khilʿa); the robe is not named.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ أَبْرِئْ ذِمَّتِي فَأَبْرَأَ ذِمَّتَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu abriʾ dhimmatī fa-abraʾa dhimmatahu
sentences.l: And-he-said to-him: Clear my-liability. So-he-cleared his-liability.
sentences.i: And he said to him: Release me from any claim of yours. And Ghānim released him from it.
sentences.n: ذمّة is a person’s standing under obligation (debt, duty, guilt); أبرئ ذمتي is a request for formal acquittal, and فأبرأ ذمته reports it granted: “he cleared his account”. The subject of فأبرأ is Ghānim, not named. The edition itself prints the hamza of the ئ in ابرئ and of the final أ in فابرأ; the hamza on the initial alif of each verb is ours.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا مَوْلَانَا السُّلْطَانَ إِنَّ الْعَبْدَ وَمَا مَلَكَتْ يَدَاهُ لِسَيِّدِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu yā mawlānā al-sulṭāna inna al-ʿabda wa-mā malakat yadāhu li-sayyidihi
sentences.l: And-he-said to-him: O our-master the-sultan, indeed the-slave and-what owned his-two-hands is-for his-master.
sentences.i: And he said to him: O our lord the Sultan, the slave and all that his hands possess belong to his master.
sentences.n: A proverb-like formula of surrender. لِـ here marks ownership (“belongs to”), and the verb ملكت is feminine because يدين, “hands”, takes a feminine verb. The unit ends where the caliph’s joy begins, in the next.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ الْخَلِيفَةُ بِذَلِكَ ثُمَّ أَمَرَأَنْ يُفْرَدَ لَهُ قَصْرٌ وَرَتَّبَ لَهُ مِنَ الْجَوَامِكِ وَالْجِرَايَاتِ وَالْعَطَايَاتِ شَيْئًا كَثِيرًا ثُمَّ نَقَلَهُ وَنَقَلَ أُخْتَهُ وَأُمَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-khalīfatu bi-dhālika thumma amara an yufrada lahu qaṣrun wa-rattaba lahu mina al-jawāmiki wa-al-jirāyāti wa-al-ʿaṭāyāti shayʾan kathīran thumma naqalahu wa-naqala ukhtahu wa-ummahu
sentences.l: So-rejoiced the-caliph at-that; then he-commanded-that be-set-apart for-him a-palace, and-he-assigned for-him of the-stipends and-the-rations and-the-gifts a-thing much; then he-moved-him and-moved his-sister and-his-mother.
sentences.i: The caliph was glad at this, and commanded that a palace be set apart for him, and he assigned him a great store of stipends, rations and gifts. Then he had him moved there, with his sister and his mother.
sentences.n: امران is printed as one word, أمر أن, “he commanded that”; we point it as أَمَرَأَنْ. The three nouns are administrative terms: جوامك (stipends in money), جرايات (rations in kind), عطايات (grants, gifts). The verb ورتب is read as active, with the caliph as subject, though the print would allow a passive. ثم نقله means that the caliph had Ghānim, then his sister and mother, moved into the new palace.

sentences.t: وَسَمِعَ الْخَلِيفَةُ بِأُخْتِهِ فِتْنَةَ أَنَّهَا فِى الْحُسْنِ فِتْنَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-samiʿa al-khalīfatu bi-ukhtihi Fitnata annahā fī al-ḥusni fitnatun
sentences.l: And-heard the-caliph of-his-sister Fitna that-she in the-beauty a-temptation.
sentences.i: And the caliph heard tell of Ghānim’s sister Fitna, that in beauty she was a true fitna, a temptation.
sentences.n: فتنة is both the sister’s name, Fitna, and the common noun, “temptation, enchantment, a cause of trial”; the sentence plays on the two. As a woman’s name ending in ـة it takes no tanwīn and a fatḥa in the genitive (here in apposition to أخته). سمع بـ is “hear of, hear tell of”.

sentences.t: فَخَطَبَهَا الْخَلِيفَةُ مِنْ غَانِمٍ فَقَالَ لَهُ غَانِمٌ إِنَّهَا جَارِيَتُكَ وَأَنَا مَمْلُوكُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-khaṭabahā al-khalīfatu min Ghānimin fa-qāla lahu Ghānimun innahā jāriyatuka wa-anā mamlūkuka
sentences.l: So-asked-in-marriage-her the-caliph from Ghānim; so-said to-him Ghānim: Indeed-she your-slave-girl and-I your-owned-one.
sentences.i: So the caliph asked Ghānim for her hand, and Ghānim said to him: She is your handmaid, and I am your bondsman.

sentences.t: فَشَكَرَهُ وَأَعْطَاهُ مِائَةَ أَلْفِ دِينَارٍ وَأَتَى بِالشُّهُودِ وَالْقَاضِي وَكَتَبُوا الْكِتَابَيْنِ فِي نَهَارٍ وَاحِدٍ وَهُوَ كِتَابُ الْخَلِيفَةِ عَلَى فِتْنَةَ وَكِتَابُ غَانِمِ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَلَى قُوتِ الْقُلُوبِ
sentences.tr: fa-shakarahu wa-aʿṭāhu miʾata alfi dīnārin wa-atā bi-al-shuhūdi wa-al-qāḍī wa-katabū al-kitābayni fī nahārin wāḥidin wa-huwa kitābu al-khalīfati ʿalā Fitnata wa-kitābu Ghānimi ibni Ayyūba ʿalā Qūti al-Qulūbi
sentences.l: So-he-thanked-him and-gave-him a-hundred of-thousand of-dinar and-brought-with the-witnesses and-the-judge, and-they-wrote the-two-writings in a-day one, and-it the-writing-of the-caliph upon Fitna and-the-writing-of Ghānim son-of Ayyūb upon Qūt al-Qulūb.
sentences.i: So he thanked him, and gave him a hundred thousand dinars, and he brought the witnesses and the qadi, and they wrote the two marriage contracts on a single day: the caliph’s contract with Fitna, and the contract of Ghānim son of Ayyūb with Qūt al-Qulūb.
sentences.n: The subjects are not named and shift without warning; the sense seems to be that Ghānim thanks the caliph, who gives the money (presumably the bride’s dower) and fetches the witnesses and the judge. كتاب here is the marriage contract, and عَلَى with the bride’s name is the idiom for “contracted upon her”, i.e. to marry her. مائة keeps the hamza the edition prints.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَ هُوَ وَغَانِمٌ فِي لَيْلَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-dakhala huwa wa-Ghānimun fī laylatin wāḥidatin
sentences.l: And-entered he and-Ghānim in a-night one.
sentences.i: And he and Ghānim went in to their brides on one and the same night.
sentences.n: دخل, “he went in”, has no object here: it is the standard word for the husband’s first entry to the bride on the wedding night, and the brides (Fitna and Qūt al-Qulūb) are understood from the previous sentence. The pronoun هو is the caliph, with وغانم added after it.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الْخَلِيفَةُ أَمَرَأَنْ يُؤَرَّخَ مَا جَرَى لِغَانِمٍ مِنْ حَدِيثِهِ مِنْ أَوَّلِهِ إِلَى آخِرَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-khalīfatu amara an yuʾarrakha mā jarā li-Ghānimin min ḥadīthihi min awwalihi ilā ākhirati
sentences.l: And-when entered-the-morning the-caliph, he-commanded-that be-dated(-recorded) what befell to-Ghānim of his-story, from its-beginning to its-end.
sentences.i: When morning came, the caliph commanded that all that had befallen Ghānim be set down in a chronicle, his story from its beginning to its end,
sentences.n: امران is again one word, أمر أن. يؤرخ is printed with a damma on the yāʾ, which we keep (a passive, yuʾarrakha, “be recorded, chronicled”); the hamza after the wāw is ours. The final word is printed آخرة with tāʾ marbūṭa where آخره, “its end”, is meant; we point the letters as printed (ākhirati), and it is not the word for “the hereafter”. The edition itself prints the madda of آخرة. This unit is an unfinished clause: the next unit continues the caliph’s orders.

sentences.t: وَأَنْ يُخَلَّدَ فِى الْخِزَانَةِ حَتَّى يَقْرَأَهُ الَّذِى يَأْ تِي مِنْ بَعْدِهِ فَيَتَعَجَّبَ مِنْ تَصَرُّفَاتِ الْأَ قْدَارِ وَيُفَوِّضَ الْأَمْرَ إِلَى خَالِقِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-an yukhallada fī al-khizānati ḥattā yaqraʾahu alladhī yaʾ tī min baʿdihi fa-yataʿajjaba min taṣarrufāti al-a qdāri wa-yufawwiḍa al-amra ilā khāliqi al-layli wa-al-nahāri
sentences.l: And-that be-made-eternal in the-treasury until reads-it the-one-who he-comes from after-him, so-he-marvel at the-turnings-of the-decrees and-entrust the-matter to the-creator-of the-night and-the-day.
sentences.i: and that it be preserved in the treasury, until whoever comes after him might read it, marvel at the turns of fate, and commit the whole matter to the Creator of night and day.
sentences.n: Two word-division slips: الذى يا تي is الذي يأتي, “who comes”, and الا قدار is الأقدار, “the decrees”, each printed as two words; we keep the printed division, pointing يَأْ + تِي and الْأَ + قْدَارِ. The verbs يقرأ, فيتعجب and ويفوض are all subjunctive, continuing the purpose clause after حتى. تصرفات الأقدار, “the turnings of the decrees”, is the vicissitudes of fate. The edition itself prints the hamza of يقرأه.

sentences.t: وَلَيْسَ هَذَا بِأَعْجَبَ مِنْ حِكَايَةِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ وَوَلَدِهِ شَرْكَانَ وَوَلَدِهِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَمَا جَرَى لَهُمْ مِنَ الْعَجَائِبِ وَالْغَرَائِبِ
sentences.tr: wa-laysa hādhā bi-aʿjaba min ḥikāyati al-maliki ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni wa-waladihi Sharkāna wa-waladihi Ḍawʾi al-Makāni wa-mā jarā lahum mina al-ʿajāʾibi wa-al-gharāʾibi
sentences.l: And-not-is this by-more-wondrous than the-tale-of the-king ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān and-his-son Sharkān and-his-son Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and-what befell to-them of the-wonders and-the-marvels.
sentences.i: Yet this is no more wondrous than the tale of King ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān, and of his son Sharkān, and his son Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and all the wonders and marvels that befell them.
sentences.n: The sentence is grammatically complete and closes the caliph's section: it points ahead to the new tale. بِأَعْجَبَ is the elative (“more wondrous”) with the بِـ that regularly follows a negated ليس, giving “is not more wondrous than”. وولده شركان وولده ضوء المكان: the second “his son” belongs to Sharkān, so Ḍawʾ al-Makān (“Light of the Place”) is ʿUmar’s grandson. The edition itself prints the hamza of العجائب and والغرائب.

sentences.t: قَالَ الْمَلِكُ وَمَا حِكَايَتُهُمْ
sentences.tr: qāla al-maliku wa-mā ḥikāyatuhum
sentences.l: He-said the-king: And-what their-story?
sentences.i: The king said: And what is their story?
sentences.n: The unit begins mid-dialogue. The king (Shahriyār) asks about the people just named, and Shahrazād answers in the next unit.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّهُ كَانَ بِمَدِينَةِ السَّلَامِ قَبْلَ خِلَافَةِ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ مَلِكٌ يُقَالُ لَهُ عُمَرُ بْنُ النُّعْمَانِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu annahu kāna bi-madīnati al-salāmi qabla khilāfati ʿabdi al-maliki ibni Marwāna malikun yuqālu lahu ʿUmaru ibnu al-Nuʿmāni
sentences.l: She-said: It-reached-me, O-you the-king the-felicitous, that-he was in-city-of the-Peace, before caliphate-of servant-of the-King son-of Marwān, a-king it-is-said to-him ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that in the City of Peace, before the caliphate of ʿAbd al-Malik son of Marwān, there lived a king named ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.n: Madīnat al-Salām, the City of Peace, is Baghdad. ʿAbd al-Malik reigned 685–705, but Baghdad was founded only in 762, so a king of Baghdad “before” him is the storyteller’s setting, not history. أنه كان is the usual opening of a tale: “that there was”.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ مِنَ الْجَبَابِرَةِ الْكِبَارِ وَكَانَ قَدْ قَهَرَ الْمُلُوكَ الْأَ كَاسِرَةَ وَالْقَيَاصِرَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna mina al-jabābirati al-kibāri wa-kāna qad qahara al-mulūka al-a kāsirata wa-al-qayāṣirata
sentences.l: And-he-was of the-tyrants the-great, and-he-was had he-subdued the-kings, the-Chosroes and-the-Caesars.
sentences.i: He was one of the great tyrants, and he had brought down the kings, the Chosroes and the Caesars.
sentences.n: The edition prints الا كاسرة with a space: it is الأكاسرة, “the Chosroes”, split by a slip. We keep the printed division, pointing the first piece as الْأَ and the second as كَاسِرَةَ. Chosroes (kisrā) and Caesar (qayṣar) stand for the Persian and Byzantine emperors; the paired plurals الأكاسرة والقياصرة rhyme.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ لَا يُصْطَلَى لَهُ بِنَارٍ وَلَا يُجَارِيهِ أَحَدٌ فِي مِضْمَارٍ وَكَانَ إِذَا غَضِبَ خَرَجَ مِنْ مَنْخِرَيْهِ الشَّرَارُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna lā yuṣṭalā lahu bi-nārin wa-lā yujārīhi aḥadun fī miḍmārin wa-kāna idhā ghaḍiba kharaja min mankhirayhi al-sharāru
sentences.l: And-he-was: not is-warmed-at for-him at-a-fire, and-not rivals-him anyone in a-racecourse; and-he-was when he-grew-angry came-out from his-two-nostrils the-sparks.
sentences.i: No one could stand before his fire, and no one could run level with him on any course; and when he grew angry, sparks flew from his nostrils.
sentences.n: لا يصطلى له بنار, literally “no one warms himself at a fire for him”, is a stock saying: no one can face his fire, his fury. It rhymes with في مضمار, and the next clause ends in الشرار. The passive يُصْطَلَى is pointed to match the sense.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ قَدْ مَلَكَ جَمِيعَ الْأَقْطَارِ وَأَطَاعَ اللَّهُ لَهُ جَمِيعَ الْعِبَادِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna qad malaka jamīʿa al-aqṭāri wa-aṭāʿa Allāhu lahu jamīʿa al-ʿibādi
sentences.l: And-he-was had he-ruled all-of the-regions, and-made-obedient God to-him all-of the-servants.
sentences.i: He had ruled over all the lands, and God had made all His servants submit to him.
sentences.n: أطاع الله له is “God made (them) submit to him”: a causative أطاع with له, “for him”. The same phrase recurs below.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ نَفَذَ أَمْرُهُ فِي سَائِرِ الْأَمْصَارِ وَوَصَلَتْ عَسَاكِرُهُ إِلَى أَقْصَى الْبِلَادِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad nafadha amruhu fī sāʾiri al-amṣāri wa-waṣalat ʿasākiruhu ilā aqṣā al-bilādi
sentences.l: And-had passed his-command in all-of the-cities, and-arrived his-armies to farthest-of the-lands.
sentences.i: His command ran through all the cities, and his armies reached the farthest lands.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَ فِي حُكْمِهِ الْمَشْرِقُ وَالْمَغْرِبُ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا مِنَ الْهِنْدِ وَالسِّنْدِ وَالصِّينِ وَأَرْضِ الْحِجَازِ وَبِلَادِ الْيَمَنِ وَجَزائِرِ الْهِنْدِ وَالصِّينِ وَبِلَادِ الشِّمَالِ وَ دِيَارِ بَكْرٍ وَأَرْضِ السُّودَانِ وَجَزائِرِ الْبِحَارِ وَمَا فِى الْأَرْضِ مِنْ مَشَاهِيرِ الْأَنْهَارِ كَسَيْحُونَ وَجَيْحُونَ وَالنِّيلِ وَالْفُرَاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-dakhala fī ḥukmihi al-mashriqu wa-al-maghribu wa-mā baynahumā mina al-hindi wa-al-sindi wa-al-ṣīni wa-arḍi al-ḥijāzi wa-bilādi al-yamani wa-jazāʾiri al-hindi wa-al-ṣīni wa-bilādi al-shimāli wa- diyāri bakrin wa-arḍi al-sūdāni wa-jazāʾiri al-biḥāri wa-mā fī al-arḍi min mashāhīri al-anhāri ka-sayḥūna wa-jayḥūna wa-al-nīli wa-al-furāti
sentences.l: And-entered into his-rule the-east and-the-west and-what between-the-two-of-them of the-India and-the-Sind and-the-China and-land-of the-Ḥijāz and-lands-of the-Yemen and-islands-of the-India and-the-China and-lands-of the-north and- homes-of Bakr and-land-of the-Sudan and-islands-of the-seas and-what in the-earth of famous-ones-of the-rivers, like-Sayḥūn and-Jayḥūn and-the-Nile and-the-Euphrates.
sentences.i: Into his rule came the East and the West and all between them, from India and Sind and China, the land of the Hijaz and the lands of Yemen, the islands of India and China, the lands of the North and Diyār Bakr, the land of the Sudan, the islands of the seas, and the famous rivers of the earth, such as the Sayhun and the Jayhun, the Nile and the Euphrates.
sentences.n: Two printing oddities: a lone و ends the line before ديار, so we keep it as a separate word, وَ, for وَدِيَارِ “and Diyār Bakr” (the upper Mesopotamian province); and فى is printed with a dotless ى, kept as printed. الهند والصين occurs twice, as printed. Sayḥūn and Jayḥūn are the Jaxartes (Syr Darya) and the Oxus (Amu Darya).

sentences.t: وَأَرْسَلَ رُسُلَهُ إِلَى أَقْصَى الْمَدائِنِ أَيأْتُوهُ بِحَقِيقَةِ الْأَخْبَارِ فَعَادُوالَهُ وَأَخْبَرُوهُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَالطَّاعَةِ وَالْأَمَانِ وَالدُّعَاءِ لِلسُّلْطَانِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ هَذَا
sentences.tr: wa-arsala rusulahu ilā aqṣā al-madāʾini ayʾtūhu bi-ḥaqīqati al-akhbāri fa-ʿādūlahu wa-akhbarūhu bi-al-ʿadli wa-al-ṭāʿati wa-al-amāni wa-al-duʿāʾi li-al-sulṭāni ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni hādhā
sentences.l: And-he-sent his-messengers to farthest-of the-cities, that-they-bring-him with-truth-of the-reports; so-they-returned-to-him and-informed-him of-the-justice and-the-obedience and-the-security and-the-prayer for-the-sultan ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān this.
sentences.i: He sent his messengers to the farthest cities to bring him true tidings, and they came back and told him of justice, obedience and safety, and of prayers offered for this sultan, ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.n: ايأتوه is printed with an initial alif where the sense needs a purpose particle (ليأتوه, “that they bring him”); we point the printed letters as أَ + يَأْتُوهُ and read the sense as purpose. فعادواله is printed as one word, فَعَادُوا + لَهُ. The ending هذا, “this”, points back to the king: “this ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān”.

sentences.t: وَعُمَرُ بْنُ النُّعْمَانِ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ لَهُ نَسَبٌ عَظِيمُ الشَّأنِ تُحْمَلُ إِلَيْهِ الْهَدَايَا وَالتُّحَفُ وَالْخَرَاجُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكَانٍ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿUmaru ibnu al-Nuʿmāni yā maliku al-zamāni lahu nasabun ʿaẓīmu al-shaʾni tuḥmalu ilayhi al-hadāyā wa-al-tuḥafu wa-al-kharāju min kulli makānin
sentences.l: And-ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān, O king-of the-age, to-him a-lineage great-of the-station; are-carried to-him the-gifts and-the-rarities and-the-tribute from every place.
sentences.i: Now ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān, O king of the age, was of exalted rank, and gifts and rarities and tribute were carried to him from every place.
sentences.n: Shahrazād turns to address the king directly (يا ملك الزمان). The two rhymes are الشان and مكان. له نسب عظيم الشان is “he had a lineage great of station”, an adjective-plus-genitive phrase.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ قَدْ سَمَّاهُ شَرْكَانَ وَهُوَ أَشْبَهُ النَّاسِ بِهِ وَقَدْ طَلَعَ آفَةً مِنْ آفَاتِ الزَّمَانِ وَقَهَرَ الشُّجْعَانَ وَأَبَادَ الْأَقْرَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna lahu waladun qad sammāhu Sharkāna wa-huwa ashbahu al-nāsi bihi wa-qad ṭalaʿa āfatan min āfāti al-zamāni wa-qahara al-shujʿāna wa-abāda al-aqrāna
sentences.l: And-he-was to-him a-son, had he-named-him Sharkān, and-he the-most-like of-the-people to-him; and-had he-turned-out a-calamity from calamities-of the-age, and-subdued the-brave and-destroyed the-peers.
sentences.i: He had a son whom he had named Sharkān, who was the very likeness of his father. He had grown into a calamity among the calamities of the age, a conqueror of the brave and destroyer of rivals.
sentences.n: The name is printed شركان; we write Sharkān. The edition prints the madda of آفة and آفات precomposed. The pair الشجعان and الاقران rhyme.

sentences.t: فَأَحَبَّهُ وَالِدُهُ حُبًّا شَدِيدًا مَا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ مَزِيدٍ وَأَوْصَى لَهُ بِالْمُلْكِ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-aḥabbahu wāliduhu ḥubban shadīdan mā ʿalayhi min mazīdin wa-awṣā lahu bi-al-mulki min baʿdihi
sentences.l: So-he-loved-him his-father a-love intense, what upon-it of more; and-bequeathed to-him the-kingdom from after-him.
sentences.i: His father loved him with a love beyond all increase, and appointed him heir to the kingdom after him.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ شَرْكَانَ كَبُرَ حَتَّى بَلَغَ مَبْلَغَ الرِّجَالِ وَصَارَ لَهُ مِنَ الْعُمُرِ عِشْرِينَ سَنَةً فَأَطَاعَ اللَّهُ لَهُ جَمِيعَ الْعِبَادِ لِمَابِهِ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْبَأسِ وَالْجِلَادِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna Sharkāna kabura ḥattā balagha mablagha al-rijāli wa-ṣāra lahu mina al-ʿumuri ʿishrīna sanatan fa-aṭāʿa Allāhu lahu jamīʿa al-ʿibādi li-mā bihi min shiddati al-baʾsi wa-al-jilādi
sentences.l: Then indeed Sharkān grew-up until he-reached the-extent-of the-men, and-became to-him of the-age twenty year; so-made-obedient God to-him all-of the-servants because-of-what in-him of severity-of the-might and-the-combat.
sentences.i: Then Sharkān grew up until he reached manhood, and he came to be twenty years old; and God made all people submit to him, for the fierceness of his might and his prowess in battle.
sentences.n: عشرين is printed in the oblique form where Classical expects عِشْرُونَ after صار له; Middle Arabic often keeps the oblique number form. لمابه is printed as one word: لِمَا بِهِ, “because of what is in him”. Here لِـ means “because of”.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ وَالِدُهُ عُمَرُ بْنُ النُّعْمَانِ لَهُ أَرْبَعُ نِسَاءٍ بِالْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ لَكِنَّهُ لَمْ يُرْزَقْ مِنْهُنَّ وَلَدٌ بِغَيْرِ شَرْكَانَ وَهُوَ مِنْ أَحَدِلَهُنَّ وَالْبَاقِي عَوَاقِرُ لَمْ يُرْزَقْ مِنْ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ وَلَدًا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna wāliduhu ʿUmaru ibnu al-Nuʿmāni lahu arbaʿu nisāʾin bi-al-kitābi wa-al-sunnati lākinnahu lam yurzaq minhunna waladun bi-ghayri Sharkāna wa-huwa min aḥadilahunna wa-al-bāqī ʿawāqiru lam yurzaq min wāḥidatin minhunna waladan
sentences.l: And-he-was his-father ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān, to-him four women by-the-Book and-the-Custom; but-he not was-granted from-them a-son other-than Sharkān, and-he from one-of-to-them, and-the-remainder barren; not was-granted from one from-them a-child.
sentences.i: His father ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān had four wives, wedded by the Book and the Custom; yet he was granted no son by them but Sharkān, who was born of one of them, and the rest were barren. From none of the other three was he granted a child.
sentences.n: بالكتاب والسنة, “by the Book and the Custom”, means lawfully, according to the Qurʾān and the Prophet's way. احدلهن is printed as one word, with a stray ل, and is probably a slip for إِحْدَاهُنَّ or أَحَدِهِنَّ, “one of them”; we point the printed letters as أَحَدِ + لَهُنَّ. The second ولدا is accusative after a passive verb, loose Classical, where the first ولد is correctly nominative.

sentences.t: وَمَعَ ذَٰلِكَ كَانَ لَهُ ثَلَٰثُمِائَةٍ وَسِتُّونَ سُرِّيَّةً عَلَى عَدَدِ أَيَّامِ السَّنَةِ الْقِبْطِيَّةِ وَتِلْكَ السَّرَارِي مِنْ سَائِرِ الْأَجْنَاسِ
sentences.tr: wa-maʿa dhālika kāna lahu thalāthumiʾatin wa-sittūna surriyyatan ʿalā ʿadadi ayyāmi al-sanati al-qibṭiyyati wa-tilka al-sarārī min sāʾiri al-ajnāsi
sentences.l: And-with that was to-him three-hundred and-sixty concubine, according-to number-of days-of the-year the-Coptic; and-those the-concubines from all-of the-kinds.
sentences.i: Besides these he had three hundred and sixty concubines, one for each day of the Coptic year, drawn from every race.
sentences.n: سرية is a concubine; the edition marks the damma and shadda in the print (سُرّية). The Coptic year has twelve months of thirty days plus five extra days, which is why 360 is not 365. The number is printed with a nominative sixty (وستون) and an accusative singular noun, as Classical grammar requires.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ قَدْ بَنَى لِكُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ مَقْصُورَةً وَكَانَتِ الْمَقَاصِيرُ مِنْ دَاخِلِ الْقَصْرِ فَإِنَّهُ بَنَى اِثْنَى عَشَرَ قَصْرًا عَلَى عَدَدِ شُهُورِ السَّنَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna qad banā li-kulli wāḥidatin minhunna maqṣūratan wa-kānati al-maqāṣīru min dākhili al-qaṣri fa-innahu banā ithnay ʿashara qaṣran ʿalā ʿadadi shuhūri al-sanati
sentences.l: And-he-was had he-built for-each one of-them a-chamber, and-were the-chambers from inside-of the-palace; for-he built twelve palace according-to number-of months-of the-year.
sentences.i: He had built a chamber for each of them, and the chambers were within the palace; for he had built twelve palaces, after the number of the months of the year.
sentences.n: اثنى عشر is printed with a final ى (ithnay ʿashar, “twelve”); we point the letters as printed.

sentences.t: وَجَعَلَ فِي كُلِّ قَصْرٍ ثَلَٰثِينَ مَقْصُورَةً فَكَانَتْ جُمْلَةُ الْمَقَاصِيرِ ثَلَٰثُمِائَةٍ وَسِتِّينَ مَقْصُورَةً
sentences.tr: wa-jaʿala fī kulli qaṣrin thalāthīna maqṣūratan fa-kānat jumlatu al-maqāṣīri thalāthumiʾatin wa-sittīna maqṣūratan
sentences.l: And-he-put in every palace thirty chamber; so-was the-total-of the-chambers three-hundred and-sixty chamber.
sentences.i: In each palace he placed thirty chambers, so that the sum of the chambers was three hundred and sixty.
sentences.n: ثلثين is printed for thirty with no alif, ثَلَٰثِينَ with a dagger alif. وستين is the oblique form of sixty, where a nominative predicate would give وستون; Middle Arabic tends to freeze the oblique -īn.

sentences.t: وَأَسْكَنَ تَالِكَ الْجَوَارِيَ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَقَاصِيرِ وَفَرَضَ لِكُلِّ سُرِّيَّةٍ مِنْهُنَّ لَيْلَةً يَبِيتُ عِنْدَهَا وَمَا يَأتِيهَا إِلَّا بَعْدَ سَنَةٍ كَامِلَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-askana tālika al-jawāriya fī hādhihi al-maqāṣīri wa-faraḍa li-kulli surriyyatin minhunna laylatan yabītu ʿindahā wa-mā yaʾtīhā illā baʿda sanatin kāmilatin
sentences.l: And-he-lodged those the-slave-girls in these the-chambers, and-assigned for-each concubine from-them a-night he-spends with-her; and-not he-comes-to-her except after a-year complete.
sentences.i: He lodged those slave-girls in these chambers and assigned each concubine a night on which he would sleep with her, nor would he come to her again until a full year had passed.
sentences.n: تالك is printed with an extra alif for تِلْكَ, “that (f.)”; we point it as printed, تَالِكَ. يبيت عندها is “he spends the night with her”, the polite expression for lying with her.

sentences.t: فَأَقَامَ عَلَى ذَٰلِكَ مُدَّةً مِنَ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-aqāma ʿalā dhālika muddatan mina al-zamāni
sentences.l: So-he-remained upon that a-period of the-time.
sentences.i: So he continued thus for a time.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ وَلَدَهُ شَرْكَانَ اشْتَهَرَ فِي سَائِرِ الْآفَاقِ فَفَرِحَ بِهِ وَالِدُهُ وَازْدَادَ قُوَّةً فَطَغَى وَتَجَبَّرَ وَفَتَحَ الْحُصُونَ وَالْبِلَادَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna waladahu Sharkāna ishtahara fī sāʾiri al-āfāqi fa-fariḥa bihi wāliduhu wa-izdāda quwwatan fa-ṭaghā wa-tajabbara wa-fataḥa al-ḥuṣūna wa-al-bilāda
sentences.l: Then indeed his-son Sharkān became-famous in all-of the-horizons; so-rejoiced in-him his-father, and-increased in-strength, so-he-was-insolent and-lorded and-conquered the-fortresses and-the-lands.
sentences.i: Then his son Sharkān became famous in every quarter of the world; his father rejoiced in him, and Sharkān grew in strength, became overbearing and tyrannical, and conquered fortresses and lands.
sentences.n: The subject of ازداد قوة فطغى is most naturally Sharkān, though the sentence can also be read with his father as subject. The edition prints the madda of الآفاق precomposed.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ بِالْأَمْرِ الْمُقَدَّرِ أَنَّ جَارِيَةً مِنْ جَوَارِي عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ قَدْ حَمَلَتْ وَاشْتَهَرَ حَمْلُهَا وَعَلِمَ الْمَلِكُ بِذَٰلِكَ فَفَرِحَ فَرَحًا شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna bi-al-amri al-muqaddari anna jāriyatan min jawārī ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni qad ḥamalat wa-ishtahara ḥamluhā wa-ʿalima al-maliku bi-dhālika fa-fariḥa faraḥan shadīdan
sentences.l: And-it-was by-the-decree the-ordained that a-slave-girl from slave-girls-of ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān had conceived, and-became-known her-pregnancy, and-learned the-king of-that, so-rejoiced a-joy intense.
sentences.i: And it came about by decree of fate that one of the slave-girls of ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān conceived. Her pregnancy became known, and the king learned of it and rejoiced greatly.
sentences.n: كان بالأمر المقدر is the narrator's formula for fate intervening: “it was by the ordained decree that…”.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَعَلَّ أَنْ تَكُونَ ذُرِّيَّتِي وَنَسْلِي كُلُّهَا ذُكُورًا فَأَرَّخَ يَوْمَ حَمْلِهَا وَصَارَ يُحْسِنُ إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla laʿalla an takūna dhurriyyatī wa-naslī kulluhā dhukūran fa-arrakha yawma ḥamlihā wa-ṣāra yuḥsinu ilayhā
sentences.l: And-he-said: Perhaps that may-be my-offspring and-my-progeny all-of-them males; so-he-dated day-of her-pregnancy and-began he-does-good to-her.
sentences.i: And he said: Perhaps all my offspring and progeny will be sons. He recorded the day she conceived, and began to treat her with kindness.
sentences.n: لعل أن تكون uses أن after لعل, a Middle Arabic feature (Classical omits it). The predicate ذكورا is accusative, as it should be after تكون.

sentences.t: فَعَلِمَ شَرْكَانُ بِذَٰلِكَ فَاغْتَمَّ وَعَظُمَ عَلَيْهِ الْأَمْرُ وَقَالَ لَقَدْ جَاءَنِي مَنْ يُنَازِعُنِي فِي الْمَمْلَكَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿalima Sharkānu bi-dhālika fa-aghtamma wa-ʿaẓuma ʿalayhi al-amru wa-qāla la-qad jāʾanī man yunāziʿunī fī al-mamlakati
sentences.l: So-learned Sharkān of-that, so-was-vexed, and-grew-heavy upon-him the-matter; and-he-said: Indeed has-come-to-me one-who contends-with-me in the-kingdom.
sentences.i: When Sharkān learned of this he was vexed and the matter weighed heavily on him, and he said: One has come to me who will dispute the kingdom with me.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ إِنْ وَلَدَتْ هَذِهِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَلَدًا ذَكَرًا قَتَلْتُهُ وَكَتَمَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي نَفْسِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla fī nafsihi in waladat hādhihi al-jāriyatu waladan dhakaran qataltuhu wa-katama dhālika fī nafsihi
sentences.l: And-he-said in his-self: If bears this the-slave-girl a-son male, I-kill-him; and-he-concealed that in his-self.
sentences.i: He said to himself: If this slave-girl bears a son, I will kill him. And he kept that to himself.
sentences.n: قتلته after إن is a perfect in a conditional main clause, meaning “I will kill him”.

sentences.t: فَهَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ شَرْكَانَ وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْجَارِيَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā mā kāna min amri Sharkāna wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-jāriyati
sentences.l: So-this what was from matter-of Sharkān; and-as-for what was from matter-of the-slave-girl,
sentences.i: That is what happened with Sharkān. As for what happened with the slave-girl—
sentences.n: The sentence continues into the next unit. This is the storyteller's stock turn from one thread of the tale to another.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهَا كَانَتْ رُومِيَّةً وَكَانَ قَدْ بَعَثَهَا إِلَيْهِ هَدِيَّةً مَلِكُ الرُّومِ صَاحِبُ قَيْسَارِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: fa-innahā kānat rūmiyyatan wa-kāna qad baʿathahā ilayhi hadiyyatan maliku al-Rūmi ṣāḥibu Qaysāriyyata
sentences.l: So-indeed-she was Roman, and-had sent-her to-him as-a-gift the-king-of the-Rūm, master-of Caesarea.
sentences.i: For she was a Byzantine, whom the king of the Rūm, the lord of Caesarea, had sent to him as a gift,
sentences.n: The unit opens mid-story with فانها, “for she”, picking up the slave-girl of the previous sentence, who is named Ṣafiyya in the next unit. الروم (al-Rūm) is the Arabic name for the Romans of the East, that is, the Byzantines; here their king sits in Caesarea (قيسارية).

sentences.t: وَأَرْسَلَ مَعَهَا تُحَفًا كَثِيرَةً وَكَانَ اسْمُهَا صَفِيَّةَ وَكَانَتْ أَجْمَلَ الْجَوَارِي وَأَحْسَنَهُنَّ وَجْهًا وَأَصْوَنَهُنَّ عِرْضًا وَكَانَتْ ذَاتَ عَقْلٍ وَافِرٍ وَجَمَالٍ بَاهِرٍ
sentences.tr: wa-arsala maʿahā tuḥafan kathīratan wa-kāna ismuhā Ṣafiyyata wa-kānat ajmala al-jawārī wa-aḥsanahunna wajhan wa-aṣwanahunna ʿirḍan wa-kānat dhāta ʿaqlin wāfirin wa-jamālin bāhirin
sentences.l: And-he-sent with-her rarities many; and-was her-name Ṣafiyya; and-she-was most-beautiful-of the-slave-girls and-fairest-of-them in-face and-most-guarding-of-them in-honour; and-she-was possessor-of mind abundant and-beauty dazzling.
sentences.i: He sent many rare treasures with her. Her name was Ṣafiyya, and she was the loveliest of the slave-girls, the fairest of them in face and the most careful of her honour, a woman of ample wit and dazzling beauty.
sentences.n: أصونهن عرضا, “the most guarding of them in honour”, means the most careful of her good name, that is, the most chaste; عرض (ʿirḍ) is a person's honour and reputation. The superlatives أجمل, أحسن, أصون take the following noun (وجها, عرضا) as an accusative of respect.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ تَخْدُمُ الْمَلِكَ لَيْلَةَ مَبِيتِهِ عِنْدَهَا وَتَقُولُ لَهُ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ كُنْتُ أَشْتَهِي مِنْ إِلَهِ السَّمَاءِ أَنْ يَرْزُقَكَ مِنِّي وَلَدًا ذَكَرًا حَتَّى إِنِّي أُحْسِنَ تَرْبِيَتَهُ وَأُبَالِغَ فِي أَدَبِهِ وَصِيَانَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kānat takhdumu al-malika laylata mabītihi ʿindahā wa-taqūlu lahu ayyuhā al-maliku kuntu ashtahī min ilāhi al-samāʾi an yarzuqaka minnī waladan dhakaran ḥattā innī uḥsina tarbiyatahu wa-ubāligha fī adabihi wa-ṣiyānatihi
sentences.l: And-she-was serving the-king the-night-of his-spending-the-night with-her, and-saying to-him: O-you the-king, I-was desiring from god-of the-sky that he-provide-you from-me a-child male, so-that-indeed-I (might)-do-well his-upbringing and-go-far in his-training and-his-safeguarding.
sentences.i: She would attend the king on the night he spent with her, and she would say to him: O king, I used to long for the God of heaven to grant you a son by me, so that I might bring him up well and take great pains with his training and his protection.
sentences.n: إله السماء, “the God of heaven”, is how the Christian Ṣafiyya names God. اشتهي من … ان يرزقك is a Middle Arabic construction: اشتهى normally takes its object directly, while here it works like “ask from God that He grant”. حتى اني احسن, “so that I (might) do well”, is also loose: after حتى إنّ a subjunctive احسن is printed, and we point it as the subjunctive أُحْسِنَ, parallel to وأبالغ.

sentences.t: فَيَفْرَجُ الْمَلِكُ وَيُعْجِبُهُ ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامُ فَلَا زَالَتْ كَذَلِكَ حَتَّى كَمَلَتْ أَشْهُرُهَا فَجَلَسَتْ عَلَى كُرْسِيِّ الْوِلَادَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-yafraju al-maliku wa-yuʿjibuhu dhālika al-kalāmu fa-lā zālat kadhālika ḥattā kamalat ashhuruhā fa-jalasat ʿalā kursiyyi al-wilādati
sentences.l: So-is-eased the-king, and-pleases-him that the-speech; and-not ceased she thus until completed her-months; so-she-sat upon chair-of the-birthing.
sentences.i: The king would be gladdened, and those words pleased him. So she continued until her months were complete, and she sat upon the birthing-stool.
sentences.n: The verb is printed with a jīm, فيفرج. It is probably a slip for فيفرح, “rejoices”, since the sense is that the king is cheered. We keep the printed letters and point them as an intransitive “is eased, relieved” (فَرَجَ, said of a worry lifting); this is a reading by sense, not a certain one. فلا زالت كذلك, literally “she did not cease thus”, is the stock way to say “she went on so”: a negated perfect with زال means “continued”.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ فِي مُدَّةِ حَمْلِهَا عَلَى صَلَاحٍ تَقُومُ وَتُحْسِنُ الْعِبَادَةَ وَتَدْعُو اللَّهَ بِأَنْ يَرْزُقَهَا بِوَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ وَيُسَهِّلَ عَلَيْهَا وِلَادَتَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kānat fī muddati ḥamlihā ʿalā ṣalāḥin taqūmu wa-tuḥsinu al-ʿibādata wa-tadʿū Allāha bi-an yarzuqahā bi-waladin ṣāliḥin wa-yusahhila ʿalayhā wilādatahu
sentences.l: And-she-was in period-of her-pregnancy upon righteousness, rising (to prayer) and-doing-well the-worship, and-calling God that he-provide-her with-a-child righteous and-ease for-her his-birth.
sentences.i: Throughout her pregnancy she lived in righteousness, rising to pray and keeping up her devotions well, and she called upon God to grant her a righteous child and to make his birth easy for her.
sentences.n: على صلاح, “upon righteousness”, means “in a state of piety”. دعا بأن يرزقها has the prayer's content introduced by بِأَنْ and the gift by بِـ (رزقها بولد), where Classical would give the gift as a direct object. ولادته is “his birth”, the masculine suffix pointing to the child she hoped for.

sentences.t: فَتَقَبَّلَ اللَّهُ مِنْهَا دُعَاءَهَا وَكَانَ الْمَلِكُ قَدْ وَكَّلَ بِهَا خَادِمًا يُخْبِرُهُ بِمَا تَضَعُهُ هَلْ هُوَ ذَكَرٌ أَوْ أُنْثَى
sentences.tr: fa-taqabbala Allāhu minhā duʿāʾahā wa-kāna al-maliku qad wakkala bihā khādiman yukhbiruhu bi-mā taḍaʿuhu hal huwa dhakarun aw unthā
sentences.l: So-accepted God from-her her-prayer; and-the-king had appointed over-her a-servant informing-him of-what she-bears: whether it (is) male or female.
sentences.i: God accepted her prayer. The king had set a servant over her, to bring him word of what she bore, whether a boy or a girl.
sentences.n: هل هو ذكر او انثى uses هل to ask an indirect question, “whether it is male or female”; Classical would use أَ … أَمْ or إِنْ. This is a common Middle Arabic feature.

sentences.t: وَكَذَلِكَ وَلَدُهُ شَرْكَانُ أَرْسَلَ مَنْ يُعَرِّفُهُ بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-kadhālika waladuhu Sharkānu arsala man yuʿarrifuhu bi-dhālika
sentences.l: And-likewise his-son Sharkān sent one-who informs-him of-that.
sentences.i: His son Sharkān likewise sent someone to bring him word of it.
sentences.n: The subject, “his son Sharkān”, is put first as a topic and the verb follows. عرّفه بـ is “inform him of”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْ صَفِيَّةُ ذَلِكَ الْمَوْلُودَ فَتَّشَتْهُ الْقَوَابِلُ فَوَجَدْنَهُ بِنْتًا بِوَجْهٍ أَبْهَى مِنَ الْقَمَرِ فَأَعْلَمْنَ بِهَا الْحَاضِرِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waḍaʿat Ṣafiyyatu dhālika al-mawlūda fattashathu al-qawābilu fa-wajadnahu bintan bi-wajhin abhā mina al-qamari fa-aʿlamna bihā al-ḥāḍirīna
sentences.l: And-when bore Ṣafiyya that newborn, examined-it the-midwives; so-they-found-it a-girl, with-a-face brighter than the-moon; so-they-informed of-her the-present-ones.
sentences.i: When Ṣafiyya had given birth to the child, the midwives examined it and found a girl, with a face more radiant than the moon, and they announced her to those present.
sentences.n: المولود, “the newborn”, is grammatically masculine, so the midwives’ pronoun is masculine (فتشته, فوجدنه) until they learn the child is a girl, after which the pronoun turns feminine (بها). The jawāb of لمّا is the first fa- verb, فتشته. The feminine plural -na verbs (فوجدنه, فاعلمن) agree with القوابل.

sentences.t: وَعَادَ رَسُولُ الْمَلِكِ وَأَخْبَرَهُ وَكَذَلِكَ رَسُولُ شَرْكَانَ أَخْبَرَهُ بِذَلِكَ فَفَرِحَ فَرَحًا شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: wa-ʿāda rasūlu al-maliki wa-akhbarahu wa-kadhālika rasūlu Sharkāna akhbarahu bi-dhālika fa-fariḥa faraḥan shadīdan
sentences.l: And-returned messenger-of the-king and-informed-him; and-likewise messenger-of Sharkān informed-him of-that; so-he-rejoiced a-rejoicing intense.
sentences.i: The king’s messenger came back and told him, and Sharkān’s messenger likewise told him of it, and he rejoiced greatly.
sentences.n: The subject of ففرح is not stated. By proximity it is Sharkān, whose messenger has just been mentioned, but the king may be meant as well; we leave the pronoun open in the idiomatic layer.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا انْصَرَفَ الْخُدَّامُ قَالَتْ صَفِيَّةُ لِلْقَوَابِلِ أَمْهِلُوا عَلَيَّ سَاعَةً فَإِنِّي أُحِسُّ بِأَحْشَائِي أَنَّ فِيهَا شَيْئًا آخَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā inṣarafa al-khuddāmu qālat Ṣafiyyatu li-al-qawābili amhilū ʿalayya sāʿatan fa-innī uḥissu bi-aḥshāʾī anna fīhā shayʾan ākhara
sentences.l: And-when departed the-servants, said Ṣafiyya to-the-midwives: Give-respite upon-me an-hour, for-indeed-I feel with-my-innards that in-her something other.
sentences.i: When the attendants had gone, Ṣafiyya said to the midwives: Give me a little while, for I feel in my womb that there is something more within me.
sentences.n: أمهلوا عليّ: أمهل normally takes a direct object (أَمْهِلُونِي), and here عليّ, “upon me”, stands in its place. The edition prints a shadda on عليّ and we keep it. أحشائي are my “innards”, here the womb. فيها, “in her”, is the womb or herself, spoken in the third person.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَأَوَّهَتْ وَجَاءَهَا الطَّلْقُ ثَانِيًا وَسَهَّلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهَا وَوَضَعَتْ مَوْلُودًا ثَانِيًا
sentences.tr: thumma taʾawwahat wa-jāʾahā al-ṭalqu thāniyan wa-sahhala Allāhu ʿalayhā wa-waḍaʿat mawlūdan thāniyan
sentences.l: Then she-groaned, and-came-to-her the-labour-pain secondly, and-eased God upon-her, and-she-bore a-newborn second.
sentences.i: Then she groaned, and the pains of labour came upon her a second time. God made it easy for her, and she bore a second child.
sentences.n: ثانيا is used twice with different jobs: first as an adverb, “a second time”, then as an adjective of مولودا, “a second newborn”. The edition prints the shadda of تاوّهت.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَتْ إِلَيْهِ الْقَوَابِلُ فَوَجَدْنَهُ وَلَدًا ذَكَرًا يُشْبِهُ الْبَدْرَ بِجَبِينٍ أَزْهَرَ وَخَدٍّ أَحْمَرَ مُوَرَّدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓarat ilayhi al-qawābilu fa-wajadnahu waladan dhakaran yushbihu al-badra bi-jabīnin azhara wa-khaddin aḥmara muwarradin
sentences.l: So-looked at-him the-midwives, and-found-him a-child male, resembling the-full-moon, with-a-brow radiant and-a-cheek red rose-tinted.
sentences.i: The midwives looked at him and found a boy, like the full moon, with a shining brow and a red, rose-flushed cheek.
sentences.n: أزهر, “radiant”, is the bright, shining white of a brow; مورد is “rose-tinted”, of a cheek flushed like a rose (ورد). ولدا ذكرا, “a male child”, is a common pleonasm. The verb نظرت is singular with the plural القوابل after it.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَتْ بِهِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَالْخَدَمُ وَالْحَشَمُ وَكُلُّ مَنْ حَضَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥat bihi al-jāriyatu wa-al-khadamu wa-al-ḥashamu wa-kullu man ḥaḍara
sentences.l: So-rejoiced in-him the-slave-girl and-the-servants and-the-retinue and-every one-who was-present.
sentences.i: The slave-girl rejoiced in him, and so did the servants and retainers and all who were present.
sentences.n: الجارية, “the slave-girl”, is Ṣafiyya herself, who is a slave-concubine of the king. فرح بـ is “rejoice in”. الخدم and الحشم are household servants and retainers.

sentences.t: وَرَمَتْ صَفِيَّةُ الْخَلَاصَ وَقَدْ أَطْلَقُوا الزَّغَارِيتَ فِى الْقَصْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-ramat Ṣafiyyatu al-khalāṣa wa-qad aṭlaqū al-zaghārīta fī al-qaṣri
sentences.l: And-cast Ṣafiyya the-release, while they-had-let-loose the-ululations in the-palace.
sentences.i: Ṣafiyya cast out the afterbirth, and meanwhile they had let loose the cries of joy throughout the palace.
sentences.n: ورمت الخلاص is not certain. We take it as رَمَتْ, “she cast out”, with الخلاص as “what is released”, the afterbirth. The alternative is to read رامت, “sought, aimed at”, giving “Ṣafiyya sought release”, but the print has no alif for that. الزغاريت are the women’s trilling cries of joy; فى is the edition’s spelling of في, with a dotless final letter, and we read it fī.

sentences.t: فَسَمِعَ بَقِيَّةُ الْجَوَارِي بِذَلِكَ فَحَسَدْنَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿa baqiyyatu al-jawārī bi-dhālika fa-ḥasadnahā
sentences.l: So-heard remainder-of the-slave-girls of-that, and-envied-her.
sentences.i: The rest of the slave-girls heard of it, and they envied her.
sentences.n: The verb فسمع is printed without a tā, masculine with the feminine noun بقية; we point it as printed. Then the plural feminine -na of فحسدنها resumes the group.

sentences.t: وَبَلَغَ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ الْخَبَرُ فَفَرِحَ وَاسْتَبْشَرَ وَقَامَ وَخَرَجَ وَقَبَّلَ رَأْسَهَا وَنَظَرَ إِلَى الْمَوْلُودِ ثُمَّ انْحَنَى إِلَيْهِ وَقَبَّلَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-balagha ʿUmara ibna al-Nuʿmāni al-khabaru fa-fariḥa wa-istabshara wa-qāma wa-kharaja wa-qabbala raʾsahā wa-naẓara ilā al-mawlūdi thumma inḥanā ilayhi wa-qabbalahu
sentences.l: And-reached ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān the-news; so-he-rejoiced and-was-glad-of-good-tidings, and-rose and-went-out, and-kissed her-head, and-looked at the-newborn, then bent to-him and-kissed-him.
sentences.i: The news reached ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān, and he rejoiced and was glad. He rose and went out and kissed her head, and he looked at the newborn; then he bent over him and kissed him.
sentences.n: بلغ takes the person reached as its object (عمر) and the news as its subject. The edition itself prints the hamza in رأسها, “her head”: it is Ṣafiyya’s head he kisses, the mother’s, before he turns to the child.

sentences.t: وَضَرَبَتِ الْجَوَارِي بِالدُّفُوفِ وَلَعِبَتْ بِالْآلَاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-ḍarabati al-jawārī bi-al-dufūfi wa-laʿibat bi-al-ālāti
sentences.l: And-struck the-slave-girls with-the-tambourines, and-played with-the-instruments.
sentences.i: The slave-girls beat the tambourines and played upon their instruments.
sentences.n: ضرب بالدف is “strike the tambourine”, that is, play it; لعب بالآلات, literally “play with the instruments”, is the common way to say “play music”. The edition itself prints the madda of الآلات.

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَ الْمَلِكُ أَنْ يُسَمُّوا الْمَوْلُودَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ وَأُخْتَهُ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ فَامْتَثَلُوا أَمْرَهُ وَأَجَابُوا بِالسَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-amara al-maliku an yusammū al-mawlūda Ḍawʾa al-Makāni wa-ukhtahu Nuzhata al-Zamāni fa-imtathalū amrahu wa-ajābū bi-al-samʿi wa-al-ṭāʿati
sentences.l: And-commanded the-king that they-name the-newborn Light-of the-Place and-his-sister Delight-of the-Age; so-they-complied-with his-command and-answered with-the-hearing and-the-obedience.
sentences.i: The king commanded that the newborn be named Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān. They complied with his command and answered with hearing and obedience.
sentences.n: يسموا, “they name”, is an impersonal plural, best given in English as a passive. The names mean “Light of the Place” and “Delight of the Age”. بالسمع والطاعة is the courtier’s formula of accepting a command, here as the people’s answer.

sentences.t: وَأَفْرَدَ لَهُمُ الْمَلِكُ مَنْ يَخْدُمُهُمْ مِنَ الْمَرَاضِعِ وَالْخُدَّامِ وَالْحَشَمِ وَالدَّايَاتِ وَرَتَّبَ لَهُمُ الرَّوَاتِبَ مِنَ السُّكَّرِ وَالْأَشْرِبَةِ وَالْأَدْهَانِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا يَكِلُّ عَنْ وَصْفِهِ اللِّسَانُ
sentences.tr: wa-afrada lahumu al-maliku man yakhdumuhum mina al-marāḍiʿi wa-al-khuddāmi wa-al-ḥashami wa-al-dāyāti wa-rattaba lahumu al-rawātiba mina al-sukkari wa-al-ashribati wa-al-adhāni wa-ghayri dhālika mimmā yakillu ʿan waṣfihi al-lisānu
sentences.l: And-set-apart for-them the-king those-who serve-them, of the-wet-nurses and-the-servants and-the-retinue and-the-nurses; and-arranged for-them the-allowances of the-sugar and-the-drinks and-the-oils and-other-than that, of-what grows-weary from its-describing the-tongue.
sentences.i: The king set apart for them people to serve them, wet-nurses and servants and retainers and nurses, and he fixed for them allowances of sugar, syrups, oils and the like, of a kind that the tongue grows weary of describing.
sentences.n: الدايات (dāyāt) are nurses or governesses, a word of Persian origin printed here with a plain yāʾ. الرواتب are the fixed daily allowances of provisions. الاشربة, plural of شراب, are drinks or syrups. يكل عن وصفه اللسان, “the tongue grows weary of describing it”, is a stock phrase for abundance beyond words.

sentences.t: وَسَمِعَتْ أَهْلُ بَغْدَادَ بِمَا رَزَقَ اللَّهُ الْمَلِكَ مِنَ الْأَوْلَادِ فَزُيِّنَتِ الْمَدِينَةُ وَدُقَّتِ الْبَشَائِرُ
sentences.tr: wa-samiʿat ahlu Baghdāda bi-mā razaqa Allāhu al-malika mina al-awlādi fa-zuyyinati al-madīnatu wa-duqqati al-bashāʾiru
sentences.l: And-heard people-of Baghdād of-what provided God the-king of the-children; so-was-adorned the-city and-were-beaten the-glad-tidings.
sentences.i: The people of Baghdad heard of what God had granted the king in children, and the city was decked out and the drums of glad tidings were beaten.
sentences.n: The verb is printed feminine (وسمعت) while its subject اهل is a masculine collective; we point it as printed. البشائر, “glad tidings”, are the drums and trumpets sounded to announce good news. The edition itself prints the hamza of البشائر.

sentences.t: وَأَقْبَلَتِ الْأُمَرَاءُ وَالْوُزَرَاءُ وَأَرْبَابُ الدَّوْلَةِ وَهَنَّوْا الْمَلِكَ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ بِوَلَدِهِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَبِنْتِهِ نُزْهَةِ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-aqbalati al-umarāʾu wa-al-wuzarāʾu wa-arbābu al-dawlati wa-hannaw al-malika ʿUmara ibna al-Nuʿmāni bi-waladihi Ḍawʾi al-Makāni wa-bintihi Nuzhati al-Zamāni
sentences.l: And-came-forward the-emirs and-the-viziers and-masters-of the-state, and-congratulated the-king ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān on-his-son Light-of the-Place and-his-daughter Delight-of the-Age.
sentences.i: The emirs and viziers and lords of the realm came forward and congratulated King ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān on his son Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his daughter Nuzhat al-Zamān.
sentences.n: وهنوا is printed without the hamza of Classical هَنَّأُوا; it follows the weakened verb هنّى (“congratulate”), which we point as هَنَّوْا. هنّأ takes بـ for the occasion, and the bi- of بولده also governs وبنته.

sentences.t: فَشَكَرَهُمُ الْمَلِكُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَخَلَعَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَزَادَ فِي إِكْرَامِهِمْ مِنَ الْإِنْعَامِ وَأَحْسَنَ إِلَى الْحَاضِرِينَ مِنَ الْخَاصِّ وَالْعَامِّ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ إِلَى أَنْ مَضَى أَرْبَعَةُ أَعْوَامٍ
sentences.tr: fa-shakarahumu al-maliku ʿalā dhālika wa-khalaʿa ʿalayhim wa-zāda fī ikrāmihim mina al-inʿāmi wa-aḥsana ilā al-ḥāḍirīna mina al-khāṣṣi wa-al-ʿāmmi wa-lam yazal ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati ilā an maḍā arbaʿatu aʿwāmin
sentences.l: So-thanked-them the-king for that, and-bestowed-a-robe upon-them, and-increased in honouring-them with the-bounty, and-did-good to the-present-ones of the-special and-the-common. And-not he-ceased on that the-state until that passed four-of years.
sentences.i: The king thanked them for it, bestowed robes of honour upon them, increased the honour he showed them with gifts, and dealt kindly with those present, high and low alike. He continued in that condition until four years had passed,
sentences.n: والعام is “and the common”: خاص and عام (“special” and “general”) are a stock pair meaning high and low, here in the genitive after من (we point it العامّ, not عام, “year”). خلع عليهم is “bestow a robe of honour upon them”. The verb مضى is singular before its plural subject أربعة أعوام, which is normal when the verb comes first.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ بَعْدَ كُلِّ قَلِيلٍ مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ يَسْأَلُ عَنْ صَفِيَّةَ وَأَوْلَادِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-huwa baʿda kulli qalīlin mina al-ayyāmi yasʾalu ʿan Ṣafiyyata wa-awlādihā
sentences.l: And-he after every little of the-days asks about Ṣafiyya and-her-children.
sentences.i: And every few days he would ask after Ṣafiyya and her children.
sentences.n: بعد كل قليل من الأيام, “after every little while of days”, is a loose way of saying “every so often”. The edition itself prints the hamza of يسأل.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ أَرْبَعَةِ أَعْوَامٍ أَمَرَأَنْ يُنْقَلَ إِلَيْهَا مِنَ الْمَصَاغِ وَالْحُلِيِّ وَالْحُلَلِ وَالْأَمْوَالِ شَيْءٌ كَثِيرٌ وَأَوْصَاهَا بِتَرْبِيَتِهِمَا وَحُسْنِ أَدَبِهِمَا
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda arbaʿati aʿwāmin amara an yunqala ilayhā mina al-miṣāghi wa-al-ḥuliyyi wa-al-ḥulali wa-al-amwāli shayʾun kathīrun wa-awṣāhā bi-tarbiyatihimā wa-ḥusni adabihimā
sentences.l: And-after four-of years he-commanded that be-carried to-her of the-jewellery and-the-ornaments and-the-robes and-the-moneys a-thing great; and-he-charged-her with-the-rearing-of-the-two-of-them and-goodness-of their-two-manners.
sentences.i: And after four years he ordered a great store of jewellery, ornaments, robes and wealth to be carried to her, and he charged her with the upbringing of the two children and the fair training of their manners.
sentences.n: امران is one printed word, أمر أن, “he commanded that”; we keep the fused spelling and point it as the two words it contains. The passive ينقل takes شيء كثير as its deputy subject, with the goods introduced by من, “of”. In أوصاها بتربيتهما the verb chooses بِـ for the thing commended (“charged her with”).

sentences.t: هَذَا كُلُّهُ وَابْنُ الْمَلِكِ شَرْكَانُ لَايَعْلَمُ أَنَّ وَالِدَهُ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ رُزِقَ وَلَدًا ذَكَرًا وَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ رُزِقَ سِوَى نُزْهَهِ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: hādhā kulluhu wa-ibnu al-maliki Sharkānu lā yaʿlamu anna wālidahu ʿUmara ibna al-Nuʿmāni ruziqa waladan dhakaran wa-lam yaʿlam annahu ruziqa siwā Nuzhati al-Zamāni
sentences.l: This all, and-son-of the-king Sharkān not-knows that his-father ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān was-provided-with a-child, a-male; and-not he-knew that-he was-provided-with other-than Nuzhat al-Zamān.
sentences.i: All this went on while the king's son Sharkān knew nothing: he did not know that his father, ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān, had been granted a male child, and he knew of no child granted him but Nuzhat al-Zamān.
sentences.n: The wāw of وابن الملك is circumstantial (“while the king's son …”). لايعلم is printed as one word, لا يعلم. The passive رُزِقَ keeps its accusative object ولدا ذكرا, as Classical allows. نزهه is printed with a final hāʾ where the name has tāʾ marbūṭa (Nuzhat); we point the letters as printed and read the name as Nuzhat al-Zamān. Sharkān is the elder son, ʿUmar's heir, who is away on campaign.

sentences.t: وَأَخْفَوْا عَلَيْهِ خَبَرَ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ إِلَى أَنْ مَضَتْ أَعْوَامٌ وَأَيَّامٌ وَهُوَ مَشْغُولٌ بِمُقَارَعَةِ الشُّجْعَانِ وَمُبَارَزَةِ الْفُرْسَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhfaw ʿalayhi khabara Ḍawʾi al-Makāni ilā an maḍat aʿwāmun wa-ayyāmun wa-huwa mashghūlun bi-muqāraʿati al-shujʿāni wa-mubārazati al-fursāni
sentences.l: And-they-hid from-him news-of Light-of the-Place until passed years and-days, and-he occupied with-the-striking-of the-brave-ones and-the-duelling-of the-horsemen.
sentences.i: And they kept from him the news of Ḍawʾ al-Makān, until years and days went by, he being all the while taken up with battle against the brave and single combat with the horsemen.
sentences.n: The “they” who hid the news are not named; the verb is simply third-person plural. The final clause is circumstantial (“he being occupied …”), with the two rhyming verbal nouns مقارعة and مبارزة. The name Ḍawʾ al-Makān means “Light of the Place”. أخفوا عليه takes عَلَى, “hide from”.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا الْمَلِكُ عُمَرُ بْنُ النُّعْمَانِ جَالِسٌ يَوْمًا مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ إِذْ دَخَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْحُجَّابُ وَقَبَّلُوا الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā al-maliku ʿUmaru ibnu al-Nuʿmāni jālisun yawman mina al-ayyāmi idh dakhalat ʿalayhi al-ḥujjābu wa-qabbalū al-arḍa bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: So-while the-king ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān sitting a-day of the-days, lo, entered upon-him the-chamberlains, and-they-kissed the-earth between his-two-hands.
sentences.i: One day, as King ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān was sitting, the chamberlains came in to him and kissed the ground before him.
sentences.n: بينما … إذ is the stock “while … suddenly” frame. الحجاب (the chamberlains) takes a feminine singular verb, دخلت, as a plural of the non-personal pattern may, and then a masculine plural, وقبلوا, once the people are in view. بين يديه, “between his two hands”, is the idiom for “in his presence”.

sentences.t: وَقَالُوا أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ وَصَلَتْ إِلَيْنَا رُسُلٌ مِنْ مَلِكِ الرُّومِ صَاحِبِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ الْعُظْمَى وَإِنَّهُمْ يُرِيدُونَ الدُّخُولَ عَلَيْكَ وَالتَّمَثُّلَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālū ayyuhā al-maliku waṣalat ilaynā rusulun min maliki al-Rūmi ṣāḥibi al-Qusṭanṭīniyyati al-ʿuẓmā wa-innahum yurīdūna al-dukhūla ʿalayka wa-al-tamaththula bayna yadayka
sentences.l: And-they-said: O-you the-king, arrived to-us envoys from king-of the-Rūm, master-of Constantinople the-greatest; and-indeed-they they-want the-entering upon-you and-the-standing between your-two-hands.
sentences.i: And they said: O king, envoys have come to us from the king of the Rūm, lord of great Constantinople, and they ask to come in to you and stand in your presence.
sentences.n: الروم (Rūm) is the Arabic name for the Byzantines, the “Romans” of Constantinople. العظمى is the feminine “greatest”, used simply as “great”. التمثل بين يديك, “to stand before you”, is courtly language for being received in audience.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ أَذِنَ لَهُمُ الْمَلِكُ بِالدُّخُولِ نُدْخِلْهُمْ وَإِلَّا فَلَا مَرَدَّ لِأَمْرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-in adhina lahumu al-maliku bi-al-dukhūli nudkhilhum wa-illā fa-lā maradda li-amrihi
sentences.l: So-if he-permitted to-them the-king with-the-entering, we-bring-them-in; and-if-not, then no turning-back for-his-command.
sentences.i: If the king gives them leave to enter, we shall bring them in; and if not, then his command is not to be turned back.
sentences.n: أذن لهم بالدخول: the verb أذن chooses لِـ for the person and بِـ for the thing permitted. The conditional is answered by a jussive, ندخلهم, and the closing لا مرد لأمره, “there is no turning back his command”, is a formula of submission.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَذِنَ لَهُمْ بِالدُّخُولِ فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ مَالَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَسَأَلَهُمْ عَنْ حَالِهِمْ وَمَا سَبَبُ إِقْبَالِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika adhina lahum bi-al-dukhūli fa-lammā dakhalū ʿalayhi māla ilayhim wa-aqbala ʿalayhim wa-saʾalahum ʿan ḥālihim wa-mā sababu iqbālihim
sentences.l: So at that, he-permitted them the-entering; and-when they-entered upon-him he-inclined to-them, and-turned-to upon-them, and-asked-them about their-state, and-what cause-of their-coming.
sentences.i: Thereupon he gave them leave to enter, and when they came in to him, he inclined toward them and turned to them with favour, and asked after their condition and what had brought them.
sentences.n: وما سبب إقبالهم is a verbless question, “and what [was] the cause of their coming?”. The edition itself prints the hamza of وسألهم. مال إليهم and أقبل عليهم together describe a gracious, attentive welcome.

sentences.t: فَقَبَّلُوا الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَقَالُوا أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ الْجَلِيلُ صَاحِبُ الْبَاعِ الطَّوِيلِ اعْلَمْ أَنَّ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَنَا إِلَيْكَ الْمَلِكُ أَفْرِيدُونُ صَاحِبُ الْبِلَادِ الْيُونَانِيَّةِ وَالْعَسَاكِرِ النَّصْرَانِيَّةِ الْمُقِيمُ بِمَمْلَكَةِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ يُعْلِمُكَ أَنَّهُ الْيَوْمَ فِي حَرْبٍ شَدِيدٍ مَعَ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ وَهُوَ صَاحِبُ قَيْسَارِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: fa-qabbalū al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-qālū ayyuhā al-maliku al-jalīlu ṣāḥibu al-bāʿi al-ṭawīli iʿlam anna alladhī arsalanā ilayka al-maliku Afrīdūnu ṣāḥibu al-bilādi al-Yūnāniyyati wa-al-ʿasākiri al-naṣrāniyyati al-muqīmu bi-mamlakati al-Qusṭanṭīniyyati yuʿlimuka annahu al-yawma fī ḥarbin shadīdin maʿa jabbārin ʿanīdin wa-huwa ṣāḥibu Qaysāriyyata
sentences.l: So-they-kissed the-earth between his-two-hands and-said: O-you the-king the-majestic, master-of the-arm the-long: Know! That the-one-who sent-us to-you [is] the-king Afrīdūn, master-of the-lands the-Greek and-the-armies the-Christian, the-dweller in-kingdom-of Constantinople; he-informs-you that-he today in war severe with a-tyrant stubborn, and-he master-of Caesarea.
sentences.i: Then they kissed the ground before him and said: O majestic king, lord of the long arm, know that the one who has sent us to you is King Afrīdūn, lord of the Greek lands and the Christian armies, who dwells in the kingdom of Constantinople. He informs you that he is at this time in a fierce war with a stubborn tyrant, who is lord of Caesarea.
sentences.n: الباع الطويل, “the long arm”, means far-reaching power. حرب شديد pairs حرب with a masculine adjective; Classical usually treats ḥarb as feminine. The last pronoun, وهو, refers to the tyrant (جبار عنيد), not to Afrīdūn. اليونانية (“Greek”, from Yūnān, Ionia) is the Arabic word for the Greeks.

sentences.t: وَالسَّبَبُ فِي ذَلِكَ أَنَّ بَعْضَ مُلُوكِ الْعَرَبِ مِنْ قَدِيمِ الزَّمَانِ اتَّفَقَ أَنَّهُ وَجَدَ فِي بَعْضِ فُتُوحَاتِهِ كَنْزًا مِنْ عَهْدِ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِ فَنَقَلَ مِنْهُ أَمْوَالًا لَاتُحْصَى
sentences.tr: wa-al-sababu fī dhālika anna baʿḍa mulūki al-ʿarabi min qadīmi al-zamāni ittafaqa annahu wajada fī baʿḍi futūḥātihi kanzan min ʿahdi al-Iskandari fa-naqala minhu amwālan lā tuḥṣā
sentences.l: And-the-cause in that [is] that some-of kings-of the-Arabs, from ancient-of the-time, it-happened that-he found in some-of his-conquests a-treasure from era-of Alexander, so-he-carried from-it moneys not they-are-counted.
sentences.i: The cause of it is this: in ancient times one of the Arab kings chanced, in the course of one of his conquests, to find a treasure from the age of Alexander, and he carried off from it riches beyond counting.
sentences.n: اتفق أنه وجد, “it happened that he found”, is a common way to open a story. بعض ملوك العرب, “some (i.e. one) of the Arab kings”, is deliberately vague. لاتحصى is printed as one word, لا تحصى, “not to be counted”: a negated passive used as an adjective for the indefinite أموالا.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ جُمْلَةِ مَاوُجِدَ فِيهِ ثَلٰثُ خَرَزَاتٍ مُدَوَّرَاتٍ عَلَى قَدْرِ بَيْضِ النَّعَامِ وَهُمْ مِنْ مَعْدِنِ الْجَوَاهِرِ الْأَبْيَضِ الْخَالِصِ الَّذِي لَايُوجَدُ لَهُ نَظِيرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-min jumlati mā wujida fīhi thalāthu kharazātin mudawwarātin ʿalā qadri bayḍi al-naʿāmi wa-hum min maʿdini al-jawāhiri al-abyaḍi al-khāliṣi alladhī lā yūjadu lahu naẓīrun
sentences.l: And-from the-sum-of what was-found in-it, three-of beads, rounded, upon measure-of eggs-of the-ostrich; and-they from ore-of the-jewels, the-white the-pure, which not is-found for-it a-peer.
sentences.i: Among all that was found in it were three round beads, each the size of an ostrich egg, made of the very ore of jewels, white and pure, such that nothing like it is to be found.
sentences.n: ثلث is a defective spelling of ثلاث (“three”); we point it with the dagger alif, ثَلٰثُ. ماوجد is printed as one word, ما وجد. وهم, masculine “they”, stands for the feminine هُنَّ, referring to the beads. الأبيض الخالص agree with معدن (“ore”), not with الجواهر, so the stone is white and pure, not merely the jewels; the clause لا يوجد له نظير is then said of the ore.

sentences.t: وَكُلُّ خَرَزَةٍ مَنْقُوشٌ عَلَيْهَا بِالْقَلَمِ الْيُونَانِيِّ أُمُورٌ مِنَ الْأَسْرَارِ وَلَهُنَّ مَنَافِعُ وَخَوَاصُّ كَثِيرَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-kullu kharazatin manqūshun ʿalayhā bi-al-qalami al-Yūnāniyyi umūrun mina al-asrāri wa-lahunna manāfiʿu wa-khawāṣṣu kathīratun
sentences.l: And-every bead engraved [masc.] upon-it with-the-pen the-Greek, matters of the-secrets; and-for-them benefits and-properties many.
sentences.i: On each bead are engraved, in Greek script, certain secret matters, and the beads have many uses and special properties.
sentences.n: كل خرزة منقوش pairs a feminine noun with a masculine participle; the real subject is أمور, “matters”, which the participle precedes, so “engraved upon it are matters …”. بالقلم, “with the pen”, means “in the script”. خواص (plural of خاصّة, “special property”) is the word for hidden virtues of stones and talismans.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ بَعْضِ خَاصِّيَّتِهِنَّ أَنَّ كُلَّ مَوْلُودٍ عُلِّقَتْ عَلَيْهِ خَرَزَةٌ مِنْهُنَّ لَمْ يُصِبْهُ أَلَمٌ مَادَامَتِ الْخَرَزَةُ مُعَلَّقَةً عَايْهِ وَلَايَأِنُّ وَلَايَسْخُنُ
sentences.tr: wa-min baʿḍi khāṣṣiyyatihinna anna kulla mawlūdin ʿulliqat ʿalayhi kharazatun minhunna lam yuṣibhu alamun mā dāmati al-kharazatu muʿallaqatan ʿāyhi wa-lā yaʾinnu wa-lā yaskhunu
sentences.l: And-from some-of their-property that every newborn was-hung upon-him a-bead of-them, not-struck-him pain, as-long-as the-bead hung on-him; and-not he-moans and-not he-grows-hot.
sentences.i: And among their properties is this: any newborn child on whom one of these beads is hung will not be touched by pain so long as the bead hangs on him; he will neither moan nor burn with fever.
sentences.n: عايه is a misprint: the letters ع ا ي ه stand for عليه, “upon him”, with the lām dropped to an alif; we keep the printed letters and read the sense. The clause كل مولود علقت عليه خرزة منهن is a relative clause with no relative pronoun, as Classical allows after an indefinite noun. مادامت and the two negatives ولايأن / ولايسخن are each printed as one word. In ولايأن the edition itself prints the hamza; the verb is يئنّ, “to moan, groan”, and we keep the letters as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَضَعَ يَدَهُ عَلَيْهَا وَوَقَعَ بِهَا وَعَرَفَ مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَسْرَارِهَا أَرْسَلَ لِلْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ هَدَايَا مِنْ بَعْضِ التُّحَفِ وَالْمَالِ وَمِنْ جُمْلَتِهِمْ ثَلَٰثُ خَرَزَاتٍ وَجَهَّزَ وَمَرْكَبَيْنِ الْوَاحِدَةُ فِيهَا مَالٌ وَالْأُخْرَى فِيهَا رِجَالٌ تَحْفَظُ تِلْكَ الْهَدَايَا مِمَّنْ يَتَعَرَّضُ لَهَا فِى الْبَحْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waḍaʿa yadahu ʿalayhā wa-waqaʿa bihā wa-ʿarafa mākāna min asrārihā arsala li-al-maliki Afrīdūna hadāyā min baʿḍi al-tuḥafi wa-al-māli wa-min jumlatihim thalāthu khazarātin wa-jahhaza wa-markabayni al-wāḥidatu fīhā mālun wa-al-ukhrā fīhā rijālun taḥfaẓu tilka al-hadāyā mimman yataʿarraḍu lahā fī al-baḥri
sentences.l: So-when he-put his-hand upon-it, and-he-fell on-it, and-he-knew what-was of its-secrets; he-sent to-the-king Afrīdūn gifts from some-of the-rarities and-the-money, and from their-sum three beads; and-he-equipped, and two-ships, the-one in-it money and-the-other in-it men, guarding those gifts from whoever exposes-himself to-them in the-sea.
sentences.i: And when he laid his hand on them, came upon them, and learned what lay in their secrets, he sent to King Afrīdūn gifts of choice rarities and treasure, among them three beads, and he fitted out two ships, one carrying treasure and the other men, to guard those gifts against any who might molest them at sea.
sentences.n: خرزات is “beads”: gem-like beads of the white jewel-ore described above, called beads throughout. وجهز ومركبين carries an extra و-, as printed: it should be “and he equipped two ships”, and we vocalise مركبين as the dual object. Middle Arabic: ماكان (“what was”) is printed as one word, and the plural رجال takes the feminine singular تحفظ.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ يَعْرِفُ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ أَنْ مَا أَحَدٌ يَقْدِرُ يَحْبِسُ مَرَاكِبَهُ لِكَوْنِهِ مَلِكَ الْعَرَبِ لَاسِيَّمَا وَطَرِيقُ الْمَرَاكِبِ الَّتِي فِيهَا الْهَدَايَا فِى الْبَحْرِ الَّذِي فِي مَمْلَكَةِ مَلِكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ وَهِيَ مُتَوَجِّهَةٌ إِلَيْهِ وَلَيْسَ فِي سَوَاحِلِ ذَٰلِكَ الْبَحْرِ إِلَّا رَعَايَا الْمَلِكِ الْأَكْبَرِ أَفْرِيدُونَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna yaʿrifu min nafsihi an mā aḥadun yaqdiru yaḥbisu marākibahu li-kawnihi malika al-ʿarabi lāsiyyamā wa-ṭarīqu al-marākibi allatī fīhā al-hadāyā fī al-baḥri alladhī fī mamlakati maliki al-Qusṭanṭīniyyati wa-hiya mutawajjihatun ilayhi wa-laysa fī sawāḥili dhālika al-baḥri illā raʿāyā al-maliki al-akbari Afrīdūna
sentences.l: And-he-was knowing from his-self that no-one is-able, he-holds-back his-ships, because-of-his-being king-of the-Arabs, especially-since the-route-of the-ships which in-them the-gifts, in the-sea which in the-kingdom-of the-king-of Constantinople, and-they heading to-him; and-there-is-not on the-coasts-of that sea except subjects-of the-king the-greatest Afrīdūn.
sentences.i: He knew in himself that no one would be able to stop his ships, since he was the king of the Arabs, and all the more because the ships carrying the gifts would pass through the sea that lies within the realm of the king of Constantinople, toward whom they were heading; and on the coasts of that sea there were none but the subjects of the great king Afrīdūn.
sentences.n: Colloquial and Middle Arabic features: أن ما أحد is “that no one”, with ما as a negative in place of Classical لا أحد; and the two imperfects يقدر يحبس are simply set side by side (“is able, holds back”) where Classical has أن يحبس. لاسيما (“especially since”) introduces a nominative here, وطريق المراكب, whose predicate must be supplied from the sense. The print is loose about who “he” is; we keep the pronouns as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَ الْمَرْكَبَيْنِ سَافَرَا إِلَى أَنْ قَرُبَا مِنْ بِلَادِنَا فَخَرَجَ عَلَيْهِمَا بَعْضُ قُطَّاعِ الطَّرِيقِ مِنْ تِلْكَ الْأَرْضِ وَفِيهِمْ عَسَاكِرُ مِنْ عِنْدِ صَاحِبِ قَيْسَارِيَةَ فَأَخَذُ وْاجَمِيعَ مَا فِى الْمَرْكَبَيْنِ مِنَ التُّحَفِ وَالْمَالِ وَالذَّخَائِرِ وَثَلَٰثَ خَرَزَاتٍ وَقَتَلُوا الرِّجَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā jahhaza al-markabayni sāfarā ilā an qaruba min bilādinā fa-kharaja ʿalayhimā baʿḍu quṭṭāʿi al-ṭarīqi min tilka al-arḍi wa-fīhim ʿasākiru min ʿindi ṣāḥibi Qaysāriyyata fa-akhadhū jamīʿa mā fī al-markabayni mina al-tuḥafi wa-al-māli wa-al-dhakhāʾiri wa-thalātha khazarātin wa-qatalū al-rijāla
sentences.l: And-when he-equipped the-two-ships, the-two travelled until the-two-drew-near from our-lands; so-came-out upon-the-two some-of the-cutters-of the-road from that land, and-among-them soldiers from with the-lord-of Caesarea; so-they-took all-of what in the-two-ships of the-rarities and-the-money and-the-treasures and three beads, and-they-killed the-men.
sentences.i: When he had fitted out the two ships, they set sail, and as they drew near our country, a band of highwaymen from that region came out against them, with soldiers among them from the lord of Caesarea. They seized everything in the two ships, the rarities, the money, the treasures and the three beads, and they killed the men.
sentences.n: The print divides the words wrongly in فاخذ واجميع: the letters are فأخذوا جميع (“they took all”), with the plural ending -وا of the verb printed at the head of the next word. We keep the printed division, so the first word ends in a bare ḍamma and the second opens with the stray wāw and alif, and read the two together as akhadhū jamīʿa. سافرا is the dual, agreeing with the two ships. قطاع الطريق (“cutters of the road”) is the usual term for highwaymen. Qaysāriyya is Caesarea.

sentences.t: فَبَلَغَ ذَٰلِكَ مَلِكَنَا فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَيْهِمْ عَسْكَرًا فَكَسَرُوهُ وَأَرْسَلَ لَهُمْ عَسْكَرًا ثَانِيًا أَقْوَى مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ فَهَزَمُوهُ أَيْضًا
sentences.tr: fa-balagha dhālika malikanā fa-arsala ilayhim ʿaskaran fa-kasarūhu wa-arsala lahum ʿaskaran thāniyan aqwā mina al-awwali fa-hazamūhu ayḍan
sentences.l: So-reached that our-king; so-he-sent to-them an-army, and-they-broke-it; and-he-sent to-them an-army, second, stronger than the-first, and-they-routed-it also.
sentences.i: The news reached our king, who sent an army against them, but they broke it; he sent a second army, stronger than the first, and they routed that too.
sentences.n: بلغ takes the news as its subject (ذلك) and the person as its object (ملكنا): literally “that reached our king”. The army, عسكر, is a collective noun and so takes the singular masculine pronoun in كسروه and هزموه, while the attackers are plural.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَٰلِكَ اغْتَاظَ الْمَلِكُ وَأَقْسَمَ أَنَّهُ لَا يَخْرُجُ إِلَيْهِمْ إِلَّا بِنَفْسِهِ فِي جَمِيعِ عَسْكَرِهِ وَأَنَّهُ لَا يَعُودُ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّى يَتْرُكَ قَيْسَارِيَةَ الْأَرْمَنِ خَرَابًا وَيَتْرُكَ أَرْضَهَا وَجَمِيعَ الْبِلَادِ الَّتِي يَحْكُمُ عَلَيْهَا مَلِكُهَا خَرَابًا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ightāẓa al-maliku wa-aqsama annahu lā yakhruju ilayhim illā bi-nafsihi fī jamīʿi ʿaskarihi wa-annahu lā yaʿūdu ʿanhum ḥattā yatruka Qaysāriyyata al-Armani kharāban wa-yatruka arḍahā wa-jamīʿa al-bilādi allatī yaḥkumu ʿalayhā malikuhā kharāban
sentences.l: So at that was-enraged the-king, and-swore that-he not he-goes-out to-them except by-his-self in all-of his-army, and-that-he not he-returns from-them until he-leaves Caesarea-of the-Armenians ruin, and-leaves its-land and-all-of the-lands which he-rules over-them its-king ruin.
sentences.i: At that the king was seized with rage and swore that he would march out against them only in person, with all his army, and that he would not turn back from them until he had left Caesarea of the Armenians a ruin, and its land too, and all the lands its king rules over.
sentences.n: The oath has two parts, each introduced by أنه: he will go out in person, and he will not return until he has made a ruin of the city. The single خرابا at the end of the second half serves all three things laid waste: the city, its land and all the lands its king rules. الأرمن is “the Armenians”.

sentences.t: وَالْمُرَادُ مِنْ صَاحِبِ الْعَصْرِ وَالْأَوَانِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ مَلِكِ بَغْدَادَ وَخُرَاسَانَ أَنْ يَمُدَّنَا بِعَسْكَرٍ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ حَتَّى يَصِيرَ لَهُ الْفَخْرُ
sentences.tr: wa-al-murādu min ṣāḥibi al-ʿaṣri wa-al-awāni al-maliki ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni maliki Baghdāda wa-Khurāsāna an yamuddanā bi-ʿaskarin min ʿindihi ḥattā yaṣīra lahu al-fakhru
sentences.l: And-the-intended from the-master-of the-age and-the-time, the-king ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān, king-of Baghdād and-Khurāsān, [is] that he-reinforce-us with-an-army from his-presence until becomes to-him the-glory.
sentences.i: What we ask of the master of the age and the hour, King ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān, lord of Baghdad and Khurasan, is that he reinforce us with an army of his own, so that the glory may be his.
sentences.n: صاحب العصر والأوان, “master of the age and the time”, is a courtly title of address. المراد (“the thing intended”) opens the envoys' actual request. مد with بـ means to supply or reinforce someone with something; the verb is يمدنا, “he reinforces us”.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ أَرْسَلَ إِلَيْكَ مَلِكُنَا مَعَنَاشَيْئًا مِنْ أَنْوَاعِ الْهَدَايَا وَيَسْأَلُ مِنْ إِنْعَامِ الْمَلِكِ قَبُولَهَا وَالتَّفَضُّلَ عَلَيْهِ بِالْإِسْعَافِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad arsala ilayka malikunā maʿanā shayʾan min anwāʿi al-hadāyā wa-yasʾalu min inʿāmi al-maliki qabūlahā wa-al-tafaḍḍula ʿalayhi bi-al-isʿāfi
sentences.l: And-already sent to-you our-king, with-us, something of kinds-of the-gifts, and-he-asks from the-bounty-of the-king their-acceptance and-the-condescending upon-him with-the-assistance.
sentences.i: Our king has sent you, by our hands, a share of gifts of various kinds, and he asks of the king's bounty that he accept them and favour him with his help.
sentences.n: معناشيئا is printed as one word: it is معنا شيئا, “with us something”. The envoys now speak to King ʿUmar, and in the third person of respect (الملك) as well as the second (إليك). الإسعاف is aid, the granting of a request.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الرُّسُلَ قَبَّلُوا الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-rusula qabbalū al-arḍa bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: Then that the-messengers kissed the-ground between his-two-hands.
sentences.i: Then the envoys kissed the ground before him.
sentences.n: بين يديه, “between his two hands”, is the ordinary way of saying “in front of him, in his presence”.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَ—احِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahra Zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And-overtook Shahr Zād the-morning, so-she-fell-silent from the-speech the-permitted.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, holding back from the speech she was allowed.
sentences.n: The night-closing formula. The edition prints the name as two words and has a long dash inside المباح (the-permitted); we keep the dash as printed and read the word as المباح, “permitted”, the stock epithet of Shahrazād's storytelling. Note the order: the morning is the grammatical subject, and Shahrazād, who is overtaken, the object.
